key: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly.
s: After a curse on those given a portion of the Scripture who favoured idolaters, the passage turns to trusts and judgement; al-Tabari, on 4:58, reads it as spoken to rulers, the shepherd charged with his flock as the next verse charges the flock with obedience.

evidence.words: وأولى هذه الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك عندي، قولُ من قال: هو خطاب من الله ولاةَ أمور المسلمين بأداء الأمانة إلى من وَلُوا أمره في فيئهم وحقوقهم، وما ائتمنوا عليه من أمورهم، بالعدل بينهم في القضية، والقَسْم بينهم بالسوية. يدل على ذلك ما وَعظ به الرعية في: ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الأمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ ، فأمرهم بطاعتهم، وأوصى الرّاعي بالرعية، وأوصى الرعية بالطاعة
evidence.gloss: The most correct of these views to me is the view of those who said: it is God’s address to those in charge of the Muslims’ affairs, to render the trust to those whose affairs they hold, in their revenues and rights and whatever of their affairs they are entrusted with, with justice among them in judgement and equal shares in division. What shows this is His exhortation to the subjects in ‘obey God, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority’ (4:59): He commanded them to obey the rulers; He charged the shepherd concerning the flock, and charged the flock with obedience.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, An-Nisa 4:58, at 550). Plain sense faithful to day.js: 4:51 to 4:52 speak of those given a portion of the Scripture who say the disbelievers (Pickthall: idolaters) are better guided, and call them cursed; after 4:56 to 4:57 the passage turns at 4:58 to trusts and judging; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 4:58 al-Tabari reports three views and states his own preference (awla al-aqwal bil-sawab ‘indi): the ayah addresses those in charge of the Muslims’ affairs, proved by 4:59, where the shepherd is charged with the flock and the flock with obedience. The sentence carries this preference as his, without drift. He also allows that it may have come down about Uthman b. Talha and cover every trustee; the sentence’s ‘spoken to rulers’ is his stated preferred reading, so no correction needed. 45 words; entry-check ok.
